title: Signal Loom: compact per-route & per-model analytics + chart specs
creator: Maya Singh
description: Design and prototype a compact, scannable analytics tile set ("Signal Loom") that surfaces per-route and per-model performance signals in a 2x2 tile layout for the Console. Each tile is an interactive micro-chart with coordinated crosshairs and a shared time window selector. The goal is to provide rapid diagnosis for latency spikes, throughput changes, and token-cost anomalies without leaving a route/model summary page.
background: Current Console performance canvases are feature-rich but take up a full page. Product teams have requested a condensed view for on-route glanceability and faster incident triage. Signal Loom is intended for the model-route header and small dashboard panels where space is constrained but fidelity must remain high.
acceptance_criteria: Tile layout: 2x2 grid that readjusts to 1x4 on narrow widths while preserving data prioritization
Each tile supports hover tooltip, click-to-expand, and shared time-range brushing
Tiles include: latency distribution sparkline (p50/p95/p99), throughput (RPS) mini-bar, token-shed waterfall, and KV-cache hit-rate gauge
Cost overlay toggled per-tile showing estimated per-token cost and projected 24h spend for current traffic
Design tokens, color palette, and accessible contrast meet Redwood Console standards
Prototype demonstrates animation budget for transitions and micro-interactions for reviews
chart_specs: Latency tile: area sparkline with stacked bands for p50/p90/p99; tooltip shows exact percentiles and sample counts
Throughput tile: condensed column chart with rolling-avg line (5m); supports integer RPS scale and per-second peak marker
Token-shed waterfall: stacked horizontal bars representing prompt / completion / system tokens by bucketed percentile; hover reveals sample prompts from that bucket (anonymized)
KV-cache gauge: donut with hit-rate percentage and micro-trend sparkline; clicking surfaces recent cache invalidation events
Shared brush: time-range selector applied across all tiles; supports shift+drag for fine-grained selection and cmd/ctrl+click to toggle comparison ranges
prototype_notes: Initial Figma prototype wired with two sample routes (chat-route-v1, embed-route-quant)
Interaction: hover crosshair with synchronized vertical line across lat/throughput tiles; latency tooltip anchors to nearest sample
Expand behavior: click a tile -> opens the full performance canvas pre-filtered to the same route and time-range
Mobile/Responsive: on <720px, stack tiles vertically; prioritize latency, then throughput, then tokens, then cache
Performance: animations capped at 60ms transitions for hover states; heavy interactions debounce to 250ms to avoid telemetry overload
decisions: Chosen compact 2x2 layout to balance density and readability; avoids micro sparklines-only approach to preserve percentiles
Cost overlay will be opt-in per-user to avoid noise for teams that do not track token spend in Console
Token-shed will show bucketed percentiles rather than raw waterfall per-request to reduce cardinality and PII risk
KV-cache gauge placed as a primary tile for Dedicated customers where cache behavior materially affects latency/cost
tradeoffs: Compact tiles reduce absolute data shown vs. full canvas; we prioritize percentile signals over raw sample lists
Anonymized sample prompts in token-shed add investigative value but require strict redaction rules (see security review if requirements change)
Shared brush simplifies cross-tile correlation but adds implementation complexity to telemetry queries
mock_review_notes: PM (Rafael Ortiz): like quick triage flow; asks for an explicit 'investigate' action that opens a new evaluation workspace
Eng (Priya Nair): requested spec for the telemetry query shapes and limits to avoid high-cost queries from default tiles
SRE (Liam Carter): asked for clear degradation states when metrics are delayed or partial (show 'stale' badge)
Design (Aria Chen): recommends colorblind-friendly palette and a patterned fill for p99 band to improve legibility in printouts
implementation_hints: Prefer server-side pre-aggregation for token-shed buckets (5 / 25 / 50 / 75 / 95 percentiles) to keep tile latency <200ms
Expose an API parameter 'compact=true' that returns reduced-cardinality series for these tiles
Telemetry backoff: on high cardinality routes, fall back to 'sampled' mode and show sample rate badge
Cache hit-rate gauge should derive from existing KV metrics and include invalidation event links
dependencies: PM-4120 (billing: per-token cost model exposure API)
ENG-84200 (auth: role-based tile visibility for dedicated/private customers)
